scenes.text: Look at you. Three in the morning again, wide awake, chest tight, scanning for what's wrong. Can we talk about that alarm going off in you? Because I don't think it means what you think it means.
scenes.query: bathroom mirror at night, reflection leaning on sink, single bulb

scenes.text: Your alarm system was installed a long time ago. And here's what nobody told you: it was never built to be accurate. It was built to be early.
scenes.query: old house hallway at night, warm lamp, long shadows

scenes.text: Watch yourself today. The email that made your stomach drop. The pause before you opened it. That wasn't danger. That was the siren doing what sirens do.
scenes.query: hand hesitating over glowing phone screen in dark room

scenes.text: So you check the locks again. Reread the text again. Rehearse the conversation again. Not because there's fire. Because checking is what the alarm asks for. And every check tells it the alarm was right.
scenes.query: door lock being tested at night, kitchen kettle steam, restless pacing shadow

scenes.text: Some of your alarms were calibrated by a childhood that needed them. Back then, reading a room fast mattered. Hearing footsteps mattered. Your sensitivity was intelligence. It kept a smaller you safe.
scenes.query: staircase at night from low angle, warm light under a door

scenes.text: But look around. You're not there anymore. The alarm is still guarding a house you moved out of years ago. It never got the memo. That's not damage. That's devotion with an old map.
scenes.query: calm sunlit apartment morning, curtains moving, coffee steam

scenes.text: Next time it fires, try this. Don't ask, what if it's right. Ask, what would I see if I actually looked? Then look. Slowly. Like someone checking a kitchen, not fleeing a fire.
scenes.query: slow breath by a window, hand flat on chest, morning light

scenes.text: And when it's toast, and it will mostly be toast, you don't punish the detector. You thank it. It's not broken. It's early. There's a difference, and the difference is the whole thing.
scenes.query: two friends laughing quietly at a kitchen table, easy body language

scenes.text: So. Back to three in the morning. The tightness comes. And this time you say: I hear you. I'm checking. And you look, and the room is just a room, and the night is just a night.
scenes.query: bedroom at night, person sitting up calmly, soft dark blue light

scenes.text: Which alarms in your house are set too sensitive? And who set them? Don't answer fast. Walk your rooms this week. Listen for which sirens are guarding fires that went out years ago.
scenes.query: person opening curtains to full daylight, rooms brightening
